title: Mastering the Anophthalmic Socket & Corneal Reconstructions
summary: An exhaustive clinical guide covering penetrating keratoplasty (PKP), the management of phthisis bulbi, and the stepwise approach to post-enucleation socket syndrome (PESS). Designed for residents and fellows focusing on anterior segment and oculoplastic surgery.

sections.title: Penetrating Keratoplasty (PKP): Clinical Case Analysis
sections.content: Case Presentation: A limited Anterior Segment photo showing normal lids and conjunctiva, a linear central horizontal scar in the cornea with multiple small vertical scars of old approximating sutures. The possible etiology here is a full thickness corneal laceration. Management: As it is a full thickness corneal scar, patient will need an Optical Penetrating Keratoplasty. In my opinion we should try glasses, CL (soft/rigid), if vision still poor we may go for PKP.

rows: 1. Scleral perforation (bridal/scleral ring placement). 2. Donor damage – Trephine reversal: causes hyperopia/wound closure difficulty. 3. Retained Descemet’s (double AC postop day 1 - needs re-grafting). 4. Iris-lens damage. 5. AC hemorrhage. 6. Suprachoroidal expulsive hemorrhage.

1. Wound leaks (Seidel +): BCL or resuturing. 2. Epithelial defect: Lubricants, antibiotics, BCL, tarsorrhaphy, reduce steroids. 3. Filamentary keratitis. 4. Suture issues: Infection, Immune infiltrates (recipient side, treat with steroids/removal), Endophthalmitis, Kaye dots (non-pathologic donor side dots). 5. Glaucoma. 6. Anterior synechiae. 7. Pupillary block. 8. Urrets-Zavalia pupil (irregular pupil, iris atrophy, ectropion uvea). 9. Subcapsular opacities.
1. Graft failure: Rejection, poor donor quality, trauma, flat AC, HSV reactivation. 2. Post-operative astigmatism.

sections.title: Immunologic Graft Rejection: Differential Patterns
content: Epithelial Rejection: Elevated line staining with fluorescein; responds to topical steroids.
Subepithelial Infiltrates: Immune reaction in donor tissue ONLY; no conjunctivitis; responds to steroids.
Endothelial Rejection (Khodadoust line): KPs at leading edge, hazy stroma, DM folds. Does not cross graft-host junction. Treat with intensive topical/IV steroids.
Diffuse Endothelial Rejection: Scattered KPs limited to donor endothelium + AC reaction. Treat with intensive steroids.

branches: Vascular (ROP, OIS, Coats, PDR, Sickle Cell)
Congenital (PHPV, Peters' Anomaly Type 2, Norrie, FEVR)

sections.title: Pre-PKP Assessment & Prognosis
content: History: Past BCVA, Age of Insult, Ocular Alignment, Projection of rays.
Lids & Surface: Blepharitis, Ectropion, Entropion, Trichiasis, Dry eye (TBUT/Schirmer), Inflammation.
Cornea & AC: Scar size/depth, Vascularization, PAC, lens status, vitreous presence.
Posterior: IOP measurement, DFE.
Investigations: ASOCT, UBM.
Favorable Prognosis: Keratoconus, localized scars, dystrophies.

sections.title: High Risk Factors for Graft Rejection
Phthisis Bulbi: Pathology & Identification
content: Identification: End-stage response to injury, shrunk, non-functional eye.
Characteristic Changes: Small, soft, collapsed globe; Opaque/thickened cornea.
Internal Changes: Iris neovascularization, cataract, cyclitic membrane, ciliochoroidal/retinal detachment.
Late Stage: Osseous metaplasia (intraocular bone).
Mechanism: Hypotony, deranged blood-ocular barrier, cytokines/angiogenic factors.
Management: Alleviating pain; Enucleation/Evisceration + Prosthesis (No vision restoration).

rows: 1. Primary Intraocular Malignancy (RB, Melanoma). 2. Painful Blind Eye (Glaucoma). 3. Severe Trauma (Sympathetic Ophthalmia risk). 4. Unsightly blind eye. 5. Phthisis/Microphthalmia. 6. Endophthalmitis/Panophthalmitis.

Non-integrated: Silicone/Acrylic spheres (may migrate/extrude). Integrated: Hydroxyapatite, Porous polyethylene (Medpor), Bioceramic, Baseball, Dermis fat graft. Historical: Arruga (exposed integrated).

sections.title: Post-Enucleation Socket Syndrome (PESS)
content: Clinical Signs: Deep upper lid sulcus, Ptosis, Enophthalmos (confirm with Hertel/Birds-eye view).
Prosthesis Signs: Posterior displacement, superior rotation, backward tilting, ectropion.
Lid/Socket: Horizontal laxity, forniceal shortening, Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis (GPC) from friction.
Diagnosis: Confirmed by inspection of motility and examination of conjunctiva/implant under prosthesis.

sections.title: Stepwise Management of PESS
content: Step 1: Treat infection with topical antibiotics and irrigation.
Step 2: Address Orbital Volume. Replace with larger implant or Dermis Fat Graft (DFG).
Step 3: Manage Exposure/Extrusion. Small: Direct closure. Large: Buccal mucosa patch. Very large: DFG.
Step 4: Correct Conjunctival Deficiency with transplant (Buccal/Conjunctival).
Step 5: Correct Lid Abnormalities (Entropion, Ectropion, Ptosis) and Prosthetic fitting.

rows: Fornix-forming sutures, Weiss procedure for entropion
Full-thickness Mucous Membrane Graft (MMG) or Amniotic Membrane
Secondary orbital implant or Dermis Fat Graft (DFG)

sections.title: Prosthesis & Socket Red Flags
content: Implant Exposure or Extrusion (Risk increased by irradiation, trauma, infection)
Giant Papillary Conjunctivitis (GPC) from friction
Contracture of fornices (Conjunctival deficiency)
Pyogenic granuloma formation (associated with integrated motility pegs)
Dermis Fat Graft (DFG) complications: Necrosis, fat atrophy, deep cysts, donor site dehiscence
Sympathetic Ophthalmia risk in traumatized fellow eye

sections.title: Scenario 5: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1)
sections.content: A 12-year-old boy with post-operative globe removal and systemic cafe au lait spots on his trunk suggests a diagnosis of NF1. Histopathology of the pathology leading to this may involve optic nerve glioma or orbital neurofibroma. Management involves multidisciplinary care for NF1, socket maintenance, and systemic monitoring.
